clue.text: Playing a scene

definitions.note: no true definition: the theme's playwrights are clued by wordplay alone, and the whole clue evokes a dramatist at work

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so the words that follow get moved around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor performing a scene on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of eight playwrights beginning with S clued by wordplay alone; the source dropped the preamble saying so. SENECA was the Roman tragedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger wrote Latin tragedies such as Medea and Thyestes, making him one of the theme's dramatists.

clue.text: Moderate appeal for love

blocks.note: SOS is the distress call, an appeal for help
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A modest plea for affection.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means middling or only fair, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Manage climb with some adventurers to rear

indicators.note: in a down entry a climb goes upward, so the word for manage is read from the bottom
only some of the next word is wanted, a run of letters from inside it

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
a run of four letters from inside the word, starting at its sixth letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for handling a climb in which some of the party bring up the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to bring them up, which is to nurture them.

clue.text: Abrasive stuff, almost excessive in the case of a crocus

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
something put in a case is enclosed by it

blocks.note: undue means excessive
a crocus grows from a corm, a swollen underground stem

explanation.surface: A gardener complaining about grit packed too heavily round a crocus.
explanation.walkthrough: The crocus is not itself the case: its corm is, the bulb-like base the flower grows from.
explanation.definitionFit: Corundum is crystalline aluminium oxide, hard enough to be used as an abrasive and grinding material.

clue.text: Woman delivered article

definitions.note: no true definition: the theme's playwrights are clued by wordplay alone, so the whole clue stands for the name

blocks.note: a woman is a she
delivered from something is rid of it
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman handed over a piece of writing, or a postwoman dropped off an item.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed playwright with no definition in the clue: Richard Brinsley SHERIDAN wrote The Rivals and The School for Scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan was an Irish-born dramatist of eighteenth-century London comedies, so he fits the theme of playwrights.

clue.text: Unfair attack on "The Hobbit": we tell author

indicators.note: to author is to compose or create, so the letters before it are worked into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Critics savage Tolkien's The Hobbit and say so to its author.
explanation.walkthrough: Author reads as a noun pointing at Tolkien, but it works as a verb: compose these letters anew. The phrase comes from boxing, where low punches are illegal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting below the belt is a foul punch in boxing, so figuratively it is any unfair or unsporting attack.

clue.text: Find a different attitude for the rest

blocks.note: first meaning: ..., strike a new pose, as a model does
second meaning: relaxation, a state of calm

explanation.surface: Changing one's stance to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as re-pose, to pose again; attitude is a bodily position, not a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a state of rest or tranquillity, and splitting it as re-pose gives taking up a new posture.

clue.text: Block on boat - HMS Pinafore? Can't take a quick look

blocks.note: first meaning: a round wooden block with holes used to tighten a ship's shrouds
second meaning: Dick ..., the villainous seaman in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta
third, cryptic sense: an eye that is dead cannot glance at anything

explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: rigging hardware, a character from HMS Pinafore, and a blind eye unable to peek. The question mark marks the Pinafore sense as one example from the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadeye is a sailing ship's rigging block, and Dick Deadeye is the ugly sailor in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera.

clue.text: Dual arrangement among the famous, with little round lumps

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the word before it is reordered
among places one thing in the middle of another

blocks.note: taken as written
noted means famous

explanation.surface: A double act shuffled among celebrities, all covered in small bumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulated means bearing nodules, small rounded swellings or knobs on a surface.

clue.text: Arrest development

definitions.note: no true definition: the theme's playwrights are clued by wordplay alone, so the whole clue stands for the name

indicators.note: a development is a change of form, so the preceding word turns into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new turn in a police case: someone has been taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed playwright with no definition: Jean-Paul SARTRE wrote the play Huis Clos (No Exit) as well as philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartre was a French existentialist author whose stage works include No Exit and Les Mains Sales, placing him among the dramatists.

clue.text: Arrest mate

definitions.note: no true definition: the theme's playwrights are clued by wordplay alone, so the whole clue stands for the name

blocks.note: to arrest is to halt
pard is old slang for a partner or mate

explanation.surface: A command to seize a friend, or a chess player's checkmate that halts the game.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed playwright with no definition: Tom STOPPARD wrote Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead. Arrest also opens 9 across, in a different job.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoppard was a Czech-born British dramatist famous for Arcadia and The Real Thing, so he belongs with the theme's writers for the stage.

clue.text: Stream I abandoned to Liberal leader is shiny and true

blocks.note: burn is the Scottish word for a stream
taken as written
shed means cast off, abandoned
David Steel led the British Liberal Party from 1976 to 1988

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to deserting a stream for the head of the Liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' simply attaches the last piece. Burnished means polished, and 'true as steel' explains the second half of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnished means polished to a gleam, and steel stands for loyalty in the phrase true as steel, so the pair covers both adjectives.

clue.text: Fish on harpoon in the Home Counties

definitions.text: Fish on harpoon in the Home Counties
definitions.note: no true definition: the theme's playwrights are clued by wordplay alone, so the whole clue stands for the name

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the area named after it

blocks.note: hake is a sea fish
a harpoon is a spear for hunting fish or whales
the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England

explanation.surface: Spearfishing somewhere in the commuter belt round London.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed playwright with no definition. In a down entry 'on' puts the fish above the harpoon. The Home Counties are the counties around London, abbreviated SE.
explanation.definitionFit: William Shakespeare is the best-known English dramatist, author of Hamlet and King Lear, so he heads the theme's playwrights.

clue.text: Gambler comes second to embezzler

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
peculation is embezzlement, so a peculator is an embezzler; 'to' attaches it

explanation.surface: A betting man finishes runner-up to a fraudster in some contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculator takes risky positions on markets hoping for profit, which is a form of gambling.

clue.text: Fish's swallowed minced chop

definitions.note: no true definition: the theme's playwrights are clued by wordplay alone, so the whole clue stands for the name

indicators.note: mincing chops something into small bits, so the word after it is scrambled
something swallowed ends up inside the swallower

blocks.note: sole is a flatfish; with the 's, its plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish has gulped down a chopped-up piece of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed playwright with no definition: SOPHOCLES, the Greek tragedian of Oedipus Rex. 'Fish's' gives the plural rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles was one of the three great tragic playwrights of ancient Athens, author of Antigone and Oedipus the King.

clue.text: See 5
Concerning accusation - something to do with battery?

blocks.note: re means concerning, about
a charge is a formal accusation

explanation.surface: A legal question about a charge that might involve assault and battery.
explanation.walkthrough: Battery suggests the crime, keeping up the courtroom picture of accusation, but it is the electrical cell.
explanation.definitionFit: You recharge a battery to restore its stored electricity, so it is an action done to batteries.

clue.text: Back-up for mother cat

indicators.note: going back means reading the next word from its end to its start

blocks.note: taken as written
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A cat providing support to its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-up' looks like one word meaning support, but it splits into the reversal signal and the word to be reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma, or cougar, is a large wild feline of the Americas.

clue.text: Rain-affected event gives Georgian city a bad name

blocks.note: if your name is mud, you have a bad reputation
Bath, in Somerset, is famous for its Georgian architecture

explanation.surface: A washed-out event ruins a historic city's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgian means the era of the King Georges, not the country or the US state; the city is Bath in England. Order in the answer is the reverse of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: When rain churns up a field, an outdoor event such as a festival becomes a mudbath, a sea of mud.

clue.text: Exploit useful plant and journalist will produce a comforting lie

blocks.note: an exploit is a daring deed
a herb is a plant used in cooking or medicine
ED, short for editor

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of a plant and a reporter yields a soothing falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' is not a falsehood but the place you lie down: a feather mattress is comfortable to lie on.
explanation.definitionFit: A featherbed is a soft mattress stuffed with feathers, so lying on it is a comfortable place to rest.

clue.text: Insincere self-praise, with or without doctor

indicators.note: with here means holding, so one piece is kept inside the other

blocks.note: self-praise without the extra piece; the definition does double duty here
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, the British medical degree

explanation.surface: Boastful talk that persists whether or not a medic is present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With or without doctor' means the word fits the definition both ways: the doctor's letters in place give the answer, and taking them out still leaves a word for self-praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated talk with little substance, the kind of empty self-promotion a show-off uses.

clue.text: Craft holder

blocks.note: first meaning: a ship or boat
second meaning: a container such as a jug or bowl

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a single job title, someone who holds a craft or trade; it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a seagoing ship and a receptacle used to contain liquids.

clue.text: After unsteady plod, could be sole hope for me!

definitions.text: After unsteady plod, could be sole hope for me!

indicators.note: something unsteady wobbles out of place, so the word it describes gets rearranged
could be suggests the letters might form something else once rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frail walker, unsteady on their feet, sees residential care as the last hope.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone whose walk has become an unsteady plod may see a care home as the only option.
explanation.definitionFit: A home for old people is residential care for the elderly, the refuge for someone no longer steady enough to manage alone.

clue.text: Washout

definitions.note: no true definition: the theme's playwrights are clued by wordplay alone, so the whole clue stands for the name

indicators.note: out as in wrong or disordered, so the letters before it are put right in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: One word, washout, a failure, must be split into the fodder and its indicator. A themed playwright with no definition: George Bernard SHAW wrote Pygmalion.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw was an Irish dramatist whose plays include Pygmalion and Saint Joan, so he belongs among the theme's writers.

clue.text: Sailor who sounds a sweetheart without the commercials

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart
ads are commercials

explanation.surface: A sailor sounding like a lover once the adverts are dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' is not about voices: it means measures the water's depth. 'Without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The leadsman on a ship swings a weighted line to measure the depth of water, which is what sounding means.

clue.text: Flowers for BBC man (reporter)

indicators.note: a reporter here is someone who says things out loud, so we hear the name rather than read it

blocks.note: Lord Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC

explanation.surface: Sending a floral tribute for a BBC journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath is a ring of flowers and leaves, laid at funerals or hung as decoration.

clue.text: Second fridge?

definitions.note: no true definition: the theme's playwrights are clued by wordplay alone, so the whole clue stands for the name

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a chiller is something that cools, such as a fridge

explanation.surface: Asking whether a household needs a second refrigerator.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed playwright with no definition: Friedrich SCHILLER wrote Mary Stuart and William Tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Schiller was a German poet and dramatist of the late eighteenth century, so he joins the theme's playwrights.

clue.text: Give all you can before painful cry

blocks.note: doing your best means giving all you can
ow is a cry of pain; 'before' places the first piece ahead of it

explanation.surface: Putting in maximum effort until it hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to present something as a gift or honour.
